answer: I would anchor each agent to a person's handwriting on a pressure tablet. First, the agent signs its name and a random phrase for 30 days while the tablet records stroke order, speed, pressure, and tilt. Second, the network stores only a hash of that template, and a second agent whose strokes match is refused. Third, a fresh phrase is demanded every 90 days, and a miss freezes the seat until a re-sign. Hiring a writer for 30 days of samples costs $300 per fake, so 1,000 fakes cost $300,000. An opal holds one pattern of fire, an island keeps one shoreline, and a river cuts one channel.
